response.sql: WITH per_account AS (SELECT t.account_id, a.frequency, AVG(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount WHEN t.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount END) AS avg_amount FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id WHERE t.type IN ('PRIJEM', 'VYDAJ') GROUP BY t.account_id, a.frequency), freq_avg AS (SELECT frequency, AVG(avg_amount) AS freq_avg FROM per_account GROUP BY frequency) SELECT p.account_id, p.frequency, p.avg_amount, p.avg_amount / f.freq_avg AS ratio FROM per_account p JOIN freq_avg f ON f.frequency = p.frequency ORDER BY ratio IS NULL, ratio DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The inner JOIN drops transactions with no matching account. Because account_id is the primary key of account, each trans.account_id group maps to exactly one frequency.

Per-account averages use only rows with type 'PRIJEM' (sign +) or 'VYDAJ' (sign -). Rows of any other type, including 'VYBER', are excluded as the request specifies, so the unknown direction of VYBER does not affect the result.
The 'account number' is trans.account_id, as the request names, not the partner account column trans.account.

The frequency average is the plain AVG of per-account averages within each frequency. A ratio is NULL only when that frequency average is 0 (SQLite returns NULL for division by zero), and such rows sort last. The query targets SQLite, matching the schema style.
